visual_review.finding:
Pit funnel is visible in the 4 m hillshade around the atlas point; the pit interior is a compact
nodata gap. The 4 m orthophoto has a square nodata block over the pit. No other nodata in the ROI.

At 0.5 m a sinuous collapse trench runs SW-NE through the ROI with discrete collapse pits near the
GNIS bridge points (Sentinel Bridge at the trench's NE end; Ovis and Natural Bridge on the SW trench segments;
the Garden/Venetian/Brushy/Hopkins/Chocolate cluster beside small collapses to the north). GNIS points sit
within tens of metres of, not exactly on, the features. Paved roads are also visible (anthropogenic). The
trench is no longer recognisable in the 30 m simulated coarsening.

horizontal_reference.projection: Equirectangular, standard parallel 14 N, central meridian 180 E

vertical_reference.reference: Heights relative to the 1737.4 km lunar reference sphere
vertical_reference.basis: LROC NAC DTM convention; label defines the 1737.4 km sphere but does not state the height datum explicitly. Measured values (-1587..-1529 m in ROI) are consistent.

known_limitations: Pit interior (floor and overhangs) is nodata in this DTM; pit floor depth is NOT measured here.
Atlas depth (40 m) comes from separate stereo modelling, not from these DTM pixels.
4 m post spacing: features narrower than ~3 posts (12 m) are not resolved.
1.10 m orthophotos exist but are image resolution, not elevation resolution.
README lists possible SOCET SET artifacts (boxes, seams, facets); see confidence map.
Subsurface void geometry is unmeasured by any product in this manifest.

not_to_be_confused_with.reason: Covers lon 303.86-304.36 E and does not contain the pit at 303.2299 E; not used.

notes: File CRS tag is EPSG:25828, not EPSG:4083 (REGCAN95) as the file name and CNIG page state. PROJ treats REGCAN95 and ETRS89 as identical (no-op transformation); landmarks (NGBE, EPSG:4258) are in ETRS89, so the file tag is used as-is.
GeoTIFF is PixelIsPoint: elevation posts sit on whole even metres, pixel edges on odd metres. The ROI is shifted onto the tile's pixel edges so no resampling is needed.
20.4% of the ROI is valid data at or below 1 m: a flat sea surface the DTM keeps as data. It is excluded from background relief points.
